title: Effects of Ad Libitum Ultra-Processed Diet on Brain Dopamine in Humans
official: Effects of Ad Libitum Ultra-Processed Diet on Brain Dopamine in Humans
summary:
Background:

Dopamine is a chemical that the brain makes when a person expects a reward. Researchers want to learn more about how eating different types of food affects dopamine levels in the brain.

Objective:

To test how eating different foods affects dopamine levels in the brains of healthy people.

Eligibility:

Healthy people aged 18 to 45 years old.

Design:

Participants will be divided into 2 groups (cohorts). Both will have overnight stays in the clinic.

All participants will be screened. They will talk to a dietitian about their eating habits. They will have a test of how much energy their body uses: They will lie on a table with a clear hood over their heads to measure the gases as they breathe.

During the 3 weeks before participants stay at the clinic, a dietitian will call at 3 random times to ask what they ate the day before. They will complete questionnaires. Cohort 1 will wear a device to track their step count for at least 7 days; these participants will be given food to eat for 2 days before they stay in the clinic.

Cohort 1 will stay in the clinic for 14 days. They will eat as much or as little as they would like on 2 different diets for 5 days each and a normal diet on the other days. They will have blood collected multiple times. They will have 2 d ifferent types of imaging scans. For 1 type, they will receive a drug through a vein to show how much dopamine is in their brains.

Cohort 2 will stay in the clinic for 2 days. They will eat only the foods provided. They will have imaging scans before and after drinking a milkshake. For both scans, they will receive a drug through a vein to show how much dopamine is in their brains. They will have blood collected multiple times.
criteria:
* INCLUSION CRITERIA:

In order to be eligible to participate in this study, an individual must meet all of the following criteria:

1. Aged 18 to 45 years old
2. In good general health as evidenced by medical history
3. Weight stable (\< +/- 5% change in last 6 months), based on self-report
4. BMI

   1. Cohort 1: 18.5 - 24.9 kg/m\^2
   2. Cohort 2: \>= 18.5 kg/m\^2

EXCLUSION CRITERIA:

An individual who meets any of the following criteria will be excluded from participation in this study:

1. Body weight \> 400 lbs. (weight limit of PET scanner)
2. History or current self-report of conditions that may influence appetite, in the opinion of the study investigators, including but not limited to cancer, diabetes mellitus, evidence of metabolic dysfunction, changes in senses of smell or taste (e.g., covid-related), or metabolic/bariatric surgery
3. History or current neurological, mood, eating, or substance use disorders by self-report, history/physical, Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire, and/or DSM-5 Cross-cutting symptom measure.
4. Measured resting energy expenditure +/- 30% of that predicted by Mifflin St-Jeor equation.
5. Uncontrolled hypertension, with blood pressure \>140/90 mm Hg
6. Pregnancy or lactation
7. Known allergic reactions to components of the PET agent, \[C-11\] raclopride.
8. Having had previous radiation exposure within the last year for either medical or research purposes (e.g. X-rays, PET scans, etc.) that would exceed research limits. Excessive radiation exposure will be determined at the discretion of the PI and/or study team
9. Inability or unwillingness (e.g. due to claustrophobia) to tolerate lying flat on their back for extended periods of time in PET/MR or MRI scanner or (Cohort 1 only) inability to tolerate swallowing drops of liquid delivered onto tongue while lying down on bed.
10. Having metal implants incompatible with MRI (for example, pacemakers, metallic prostheses such as cochlear implants or heart valves, shrapnel fragments, etc.).
11. Left-handedness, by self-report and confirmation via Edinburgh Handedness Survey
12. Self-report of daily alcohol intake \> 3 drinks (males) or \> 2 drinks (females)
13. Current nicotine use (e.g. cigarette, vaping) determined by participant report or nicotine dependence confirmed by Fagerstrom Nicotine Dependence (score \>= 4)
14. Current use of medications or drugs of abuse which may influence appetite or have central effects, in the opinion of study investigators
15. Caffeine consumption \> 300 mg/day (roughly \>=3 cups coffee or 2-3 energy drinks)
16. Significant dietary restrictions, based on evaluation by nutrition staff and results of nutrition screener (rating fewer than 75% of foods listed as a 4 or higher score on The Food Enjoyment Questionnaire)
17. Unable or unwilling to provide informed consent
18. Unable or unwilling to adhere to study diet, procedures, schedule, and lifestyle considerations
